doc.title: Norris Turney interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997

title: Ten years of Broadway shows
summary: After leaving Ellington in 1973 he played Broadway shows for ten years, how he got the work, and the on-stage band of Ain't Misbehavin'.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: What’s it been like since then? You left them in ‘73.
In ‘73. I played the Broadway theater for ten years. I played “Raisin’” I played “Ain’t Misbehavin,” I played “Guys and Dolls,” “and “Sophisticated Ladies.” That was about ten years there.
Yeah? That’s a good steady gig for musicians.
Yeah. That’s the best you can get in New York.
Yeah? A lot of competition for that.
Yeah.
Is it the same way you get into that as it is to, you know, you get a recommendation?

Well how I got started, a friend of mine, George Dorsey, was trying to get that same show. So I just bought a new Volvo then. The show was in Philadelphia. We drove up to Philadelphia and met the leader, the music conductor. So he talked to the contractors. And that’s how George and I got it.
Did it ever get to be tiresome night after night?
Well yeah. The only show I played that didn’t get tiresome was “Ain’t Misbehavin,’” a small band.
Was that where you were right on stage?
Yeah.
Yeah. I saw that show, and they had the band right on the stage.
Yeah.
It makes you pay attention a little more.
The piano player.
Hank Jones?
Hank Jones was on piano, Seldon Powell on tenor, I played alto and clarinet. Richard Jones played trumpet. Nice little band, yeah.
Good gig.
Yeah.
